He was failing most of his classes at his high school in Bogotá when someone (2) _______________ him to apply to MIT. He had not heard of the school. To his surprise, he got in, and he went on scholarship. Mathematically, he did well. One of his professors, an acid-tongued theoretician known to (3) ____________ his audience to a herd of cows, routinely tucked ‘open’ math problems into homework assignments, without telling the students. These had never been solved by anyone. Ardila solved one. He went on to receive his bachelor’s and Ph.D. in math from MIT.
But his academic experience was also one of isolation. Part of it had to do with his own (4) _____________. Part of it was cultural. As a Latino, he was very much in the minority in the department, and he did not feel comfortable in American mathematical spaces. No one had tried to explicitly (5) ______________ him, yet he felt alone. In math, collaborating with others opens up new kinds of learning and thinking. But in his nine years at MIT, Ardila worked with others only twice.

 

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1
options: apprehensive
apologetic
indifferent
excellent
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "indifferent"

Explanation:
☛ The correct answer is indifferent because it aligns with the context of the sentence. The passage states that Federico Ardila-Mantilla was "gifted in math" but was "failing most of his classes" in other subjects. This suggests he was indifferent (uninterested) towards subjects other than math.
☛ Apprehensive (fearful) and apologetic (regretful) do not fit the context here.
☛ Excellent is incorrect because he was failing in most classes, which contradicts excellence.
☛ Thus, indifferent is the most appropriate choice as it describes a student who lacks interest in certain subjects.

------------------

Note: "Indices" is the technically correct plural form of "index" in academic/statistical contexts, though "indexes" is also acceptable in general usage. However, competitive exams prefer "indices" for precision.
